newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai copper ends up in slow trading.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai copper ends up in slow trading.

text.p: Shanghai copper futures ended up slightly on Wednesday on short-covering from retail investors, but turnover fell further ahead of the Chinese lunar new year holiday, traders said.
The most active May 1997 contract ended at 21,760 yuan ($2,622) per tonne, up 20 yuan. It opened at 21,750, hitting an intra-day low of 21,720 and a high of 21,770.
February rose 90 to 21,710, March 70 to 21,690, April 30 to 21,700 and June 20 to 21,770.
Combined volume dropped to 14,560 tonnes from 20,600.
Copper opened a little higher on short-covering and moved in a very narrow range for most of the session with most major investors staying on the sidelines in a holiday mood, traders said.
"Some retail investor's short-covering pushed the prices up but the short-term market trend remains unclear," one trader said.
"Trading became more and more sluggish with most investors preparing for their two-week holiday," a second trader said.
Traders expect copper to maintain its slow-trade trend in the last two sessions before the holiday begins next Monday. The exchange will be closed for two weeks.
Aluminium ended down. February fell 50 to 15,380 yuan per tonne, March 50 to 15,600 and April 10 to 15,720.
